name: ACH — Role or User Change Submitted by an Unexpected Maker
description:
Attacker objective
Escalate privilege or plant an accomplice account in the ACH payment system by submitting a role assignment, role revocation, or user addition as an unauthorized maker.

Attack logic
ACH privilege changes follow a maker-checker workflow performed by a small, fixed set of authorized makers. A change submitted by a maker never seen before is outside the sanctioned administration set and may be a compromised account or a control bypass.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the maker identity auto-baselines the authorized makers and fires only when a genuinely new maker submits an ACH privilege change.

False positives
Onboarding of a new authorized ACH administrator.

Tuning
Verify and allowlist new authorized makers; pair with the maker-checker self-approval detection; review the role/user change and the checker.

Required telemetry
ACH application audit (apps-*, type=ACHAPP): USERNAME_MAKER, USERNAME_CHECKER, ACTION_TASK, USERNAME_UPDATED.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. USERNAME_MAKER = the submitting operator; ACTION_TASK/USERNAME_UPDATED show the change and target.
2. Confirm the maker is an authorized ACH administrator; an unexpected maker on the payment system is high-risk — involve fraud/risk.
3. Check whether the same change was self-approved (maker == checker).
false_positives: Onboarding of a new authorized ACH administrator.
